learningObjective: Diagnose a stride-triggered recompilation in torch.compile by reading a recompile log and identify the correct interpretation.

canonicalClaims.claim: TorchDynamo installs guards on tensor stride (in addition to shape, dtype, device, requires_grad); a call with matching shape but different strides fails the stride guard and triggers recompilation, producing a specialized variant.
conditions: Default torch.compile settings without stride-relaxing overrides.
nonImplications: Does not imply every stride change under every setting triggers recompile; some modes relax stride guards.
Does not imply the two compiled variants are equally fast.

misconceptions.claim: Only shape guards exist in TorchDynamo.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stride, dtype, device, and other guards are also installed.

misconceptions.claim: Same underlying storage means no guard failure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Guards check tensor metadata (strides, shape), not storage identity.

misconceptions.claim: Recompilation only happens on shape changes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Any failed guard (stride, dtype, etc.) can trigger recompilation.

misconceptions.claim: Stride guards were removed in recent PyTorch releases.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stride guards remain in current stable releases as of the verified date.

implementationFacts: TorchDynamo guards can cover: shape, stride, dtype, device, requires_grad, class
Recompiled variants are stored in the compile cache keyed by successful guard configurations
performanceScenarios: Unintended recompiles from stride diversity can dominate compile-cache size and startup cost in production.
